data.narrative:
Itera is a Seed-stage semiconductor company founded by AJ Cooper (ex-Lyft/Uber hardware), Mattis Fjällström (ex-Verkala), and Alex Withrow (ex-Bridgewater/VMware). The target sector comprises 3 public comparables (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private peers including Cerebras, SambaNova Systems, and Etched.

Stage-progression analysis applies here as the sole usable triangulation method. Using Itera's $12M total raised as a valuation proxy and applying a typical 2.5x Seed-to-next-stage step-up multiplier yields $30M. A peer-median approach is inapplicable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage semiconductor peers in the database (only 0 same-stage, 1 adjacent-stage match found; analysis requires ≥3 comparables). Public-comp anchoring via P/S multiples is also inapplicable because Itera's revenue is not disclosed, precluding meaningful application of the 21.4x Semiconductors P/S median.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $26M to $34M, centered on $30M. This range reflects reasonable downside (−15%) and upside (+15%) variance around the stage-progression median. Key uncertainties include the absence of granular founder track records in early-stage semiconductor contexts and lack of revenue visibility. The narrow methodological foundation (one applicable method) argues for caution; deeper diligence on technical differentiation, IP position, and comparable Seed-stage semiconductor funding terms would be warranted before final pricing.
